New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair an individual's ability to have offspring who can transmit the mutation, it can spread to the other members of the population (through sexual reproduction). Allelic sequence variation has traditionally been described as a DNA polymorphism if more than one variant (allele) at a locus occurs in the human population with a frequency greater than 0.01.

options: To find out genetic differences between two individuals
To identify differences in coding DNA sequence
To identify differences in somatic cells

questions.solution: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence called repetitive DNA, because in these sequences, a small stretch of DNA is repeated many times. These repetitive DNA are separated from bulk genomic DNA as different peaks during density gradient centrifugation. The bulk DNA forms a major peak and the other small peaks are referred to as satellite DNA. Depending on base composition (A : T rich or G:C rich), length of segment, and number of repetitive units, the satellite DNA is classified into many categories, such as micro-satellites, mini-satellites etc. These sequences normally do not code for any proteins, but they form a large portion of the human genome.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What is the technique of DNA fingerprinting?
options: The use of VNTR as a probe
The separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis
The detection of hybridized DNA fragments by autoradiography
questions.solution: The technique of DNA Fingerprinting was initially developed by Alec Jeffreys. He used a satellite DNA as a probe that showed a very high degree of polymorphism. It was called the Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR). The technique, as used earlier, involved Southern blot hybridisation using radiolabeled VNTR as a probe. It included (i) isolation of DNA, (ii) digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases, (iii) separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis, (iv) transferring (blotting) of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes, such as nitrocellulose or nylon, (v) hybridisation using labeled VNTR probe, and (vi) detection of hybridized DNA fragments by autoradiography

questions.solution: In eukaryotes, there are two additional complexities –  There are at least three RNA polymerases in the nucleus (in addition to the RNA polymerase found in the organelles). There is a clear cut division of labour. The RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S), whereas the RNA polymerase III is responsible for transcription of tRNA, 5srRNA, and snRNAs (small nuclear RNAs). The RNA polymerase II transcribes precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).  In tailing, adenylate residues (200-300) are added at 3'-end in a template independent manner. It is the fully processed hnRNA, now called mRNA, that is transported out of the nucleus for translation (Figure 5.11).  The significance of such complexities is now beginning to be understood. The split-gene arrangements represent probably an ancient feature of the genome. The presence of introns is reminiscent of antiquity, and the process of splicing represents the dominance of RNA-world. In recent times, the understanding of RNA and RNA-dependent processes  in the living system have assumed more importance.

questions.solution: From the very beginning of the proposition of code, it was clear to Francis Crick that there has to be a mechanism to read the code and also to link it to the amino acids, because amino acids have no structural specialities to read the code uniquely. He postulated the presence of an adapter molecule that would on one hand read the code and on other hand would bind to specific amino acids. The tRNA, then called sRNA (soluble RNA),  was known before the genetic code was postulated. However, its role as an adapter molecule was assigned much later. tRNA has an anticodon loop that has bases  complementary to the code, and it also has an amino acid acceptor end to which it binds to  amino acids. tRNAs are specific for each amino acid (Figure 5.12). questions.solution: The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides. The a gene encodes a transacetylase. questions.solution: The elucidation of the lac operon was also a result of a close association between a geneticist, Francois Jacob and a biochemist, Jacque Monod. They were the first to elucidate a transcriptionally regulated system. In lac operon (here lac refers to lactose), a polycistronic structural gene is regulated by a common promoter and regulatory genes. Such arrangement is very common in bacteria and is referred to as operon. To name few such examples, lac operon, trp operon, ara operon, his operon, val operon, etc.  Lactose is the substrate for the enzyme beta-galactosidase and it regulates switching on and  off of the operon. Hence, it is termed as inducer. In the absence of a preferred carbon source such as glucose, if lactose is provided in the growth medium of the bacteria, the lactose is transported into the cells through the action of permease (Remember, a very low level  of expression of lac operon has to be present in the cell all the time, otherwise lactose cannot enter the cells). The lactose then induces the operon in the following manner.  Regulation of lac operon by repressor is referred to as negative regulation. Lac operon is under control of positive regulation as well, but it is beyond the scope of discussion at this level.

questions.solution: New mutations may arise in an individual either in somatic cells or in the germ cells (cells that generate gametes in sexually reproducing organisms). If a germ cell mutation does not seriously impair an individual's ability to have offspring who can transmit the mutation, it can spread to the other members of the population (through sexual reproduction). Allelic (again recall the definition of alleles from Chapter 4) sequence variation has traditionally been described as a DNA polymorphism if more than one variant (allele) at a locus occurs in human population with a frequency greater than 0.01. In simple terms, if an inheritable mutation is observed in a population at high frequency, it is referred to as DNA polymorphism.

questions.solution: The technique of DNA Fingerprinting was initially developed by Alec Jeffreys. He used a satellite DNA as a probe that showed a very high degree of polymorphism. It was called the Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR). The technique, as used earlier, involved Southern blot hybridisation using radiolabeled VNTR as a probe.  The VNTR belongs to a class of satellite DNA referred to as mini-satellite. A small DNA sequence is arranged tandemly in many copy numbers. The copy number varies from chromosome to chromosome in an individual. The numbers of repeats show a very high degree of polymorphism. As a result the size of VNTR varies in size from 0.1 to 20 kb. Consequently, after hybridisation with VNTR probe, the autoradiogram gives many bands  of differing sizes.

questions.solution: DNA as an acidic substance present in nucleus was first identified by Friedrich Meischer in 1869. He named it ‘Nuclein’. However, due to technical limitations in isolating such a long polymer intact, the elucidation of structure of DNA remained elusive for a very long period of time. It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin,proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA. One of the hallmarks of their proposition was base pairing between the two strands of polynucleotide chains. However, this proposition is also based on the observation of Erwin Chargaff that for a double stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equals one.

The base pairing confers a very unique property to the polynucleotide chains.
The polynucleotide chains are said to be complementary to each other, and therefore if the sequence of bases in one strand is unknown then the sequence in the other strand can be predicted.
questions.solution: It was only in 1953 that James Watson and Francis Crick, based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin, proposed a very simple but famous Double Helix model for the structure of DNA. One of the hallmarks of their proposition was base pairing between the two strands of polynucleotide chains. However, this proposition was also based on the observation of Erwin Chargaff that for a double stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine and Guanine and Cytosine are constant and equal. The base pairing confers a very unique property to the polynucleotide chains. They are said to be complementary to each other, and therefore if the sequence of bases in one strand is known then the sequence in other strand can be predicted.

questions.solution: Also, if each strand from a DNA (let us call it as a parental DNA) acts as a template for synthesis of a new strand, the two double stranded DNA (let us call them as daughter DNA) thus produced would be identical to the parental DNA molecule. Because of this, the genetic implications of the structure of DNA became very clear. The salient features of the Double-helix structure of DNA are as follows: (i) It is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside. (ii) The two chains have antiparallel polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5 ' → 3', the other has 3' → 5'. (iii) The bases in two strands are paired through hydrogen bond (H-bonds) forming base pairs (bp). Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strands and vice-versa. Similarly, Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds.

questions.solution: The salient features of the Double-helix structure of DNA are as follows: (i) It is made of two polynucleotide chains, where the backbone is constituted by sugar-phosphate, and the bases project inside. (ii) The two chains have antiparallel polarity. It means, if one chain has the polarity 5' → 3', the other has 3' → 5'. (iii) The bases in two strands are paired through hydrogen bonds (H-bonds) forming base pairs (bp). Adenine forms two hydrogen bonds with Thymine from opposite strands and vice-versa. Similarly, Guanine is bonded with Cytosine with three H-bonds. As a result, a purine always comes opposite to a pyrimidine. This generates approximately uniform distance between the two strands of the helix (Figure 5.2).

(III) Lactose (the inducer) directly binds to the operator, displacing the repressor.
(IV) The lac operon is an example of negative regulation - the repressor is the negative regulator.
(V) Each gene codes as such; lacZ ($\beta$-galactosidase), lacY (permease), lacA (transacetylase).
options: I, II, IV and V only
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 100-101 | Paragraph: 4 - 1,2

Statement (I) is correct as the lac operon consists of one regulatory gene (the i gene) and three structural genes (z, y, and a).

Statement (II) is correct as the repressor protein synthesized from the i gene binds to the operator region of the operon in the absence of an inducer and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon.

Statement (III) is incorrect because lactose (or allolactose) acts as an inducer by binding to the repressor protein, not the operator. This binding inactivates the repressor, preventing it from binding to the operator.

Statement (IV) is correct as the regulation of the lac operon by a repressor is referred to as negative regulation.

Statement (V) is correct as the z gene codes for $\beta$-galactosidase, the y gene codes for permease, and the a gene codes for transacetylase.

Thus, statements (I), (II), (IV), and (V) are correct.

Answer: (3) I, II, IV and V only

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The core of a nucleosome consists of an octamer of histone molecules, which acquire their positive charge due to an abundance of basic amino acid residues like lysine and arginine.

Statement II: At a higher level of packaging, regions of chromatin that are densely packed and stain dark are called euchromatin, and they represent the transcriptionally inactive parts of the genome.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 11 | Page: 76 - 77 | Paragraph: 3- 1,2,44

Statement I is correct because the nucleosome core is formed by a histone octamer. Histones are rich in basic amino acid residues, specifically lysine and arginine, which give them a positive charge to tightly bind the negatively charged DNA.

Statement II is incorrect because densely packed and dark-staining regions of chromatin are called heterochromatin, which is transcriptionally inactive. Euchromatin, on the other hand, is loosely packed, stains light, and is transcriptionally active.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Arrange the following fundamental steps of DNA fingerprinting in the correct chronological order:
A. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases
B. Separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis
C. Hybridisation using a radiolabelled VNTR probe
D. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to a synthetic membrane
E. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Refer: NCERT | Class 12 | Page: 106 | Paragraph: 2

The fundamental steps of DNA fingerprinting are carried out in the following sequence:

1. Isolation of DNA.

2. Digestion of DNA by restriction endonucleases (A).

3. Separation of DNA fragments by gel electrophoresis (B).

4. Transferring (blotting) of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes, such as nitrocellulose or nylon (D).

5. Hybridisation using a radiolabelled VNTR probe (C).

6. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography (E).

Thus, the correct chronological order is A → B → D → C → E.

Answer: A → B → D → C → E

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If a double-stranded DNA molecule contains 20% Cytosine, the mRNA transcribed from it will not necessarily contain 20% Guanine.
Reason (R): During transcription, RNA polymerase follows the rule of complementary base pairing where Cytosine of the template strand pairs with Guanine in the mRNA.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. In a double-stranded DNA, if Cytosine is 20%, it represents the average of both strands. The template strand alone could have any percentage of Cytosine (e.g., 10%), while the coding strand has the rest (e.g., 30%). Since mRNA is transcribed only from the template strand, its Guanine content will match the Cytosine content of the template strand, which is not necessarily equal to the 20% average of the entire dsDNA.

Reason (R) is true. RNA polymerase adds Guanine to the mRNA when it reads Cytosine on the template strand.

However, (R) does not explain (A). The correct explanation for (A) is that the base composition of a single strand (the template) does not necessarily equal the average base composition of the entire double-stranded DNA.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) RNA polymerase(I) Joins Okazaki fragments
(B) Helicase(II) Polymerizes deoxynucleotides
(C) DNA ligase(III) Unwinds DNA double helix during replication
(D) DNA polymerase(IV) Opens DNA helix during transcription

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
RNA polymerase catalyzes transcription and inherently facilitates the opening of the DNA helix during this process.

Helicase is responsible for unwinding the DNA double helix specifically during DNA replication by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the two strands.

DNA ligase joins the discontinuously synthesized DNA fragments (Okazaki fragments) during replication.

DNA polymerase (DNA-dependent DNA polymerase) catalyzes the polymerization of deoxynucleotides to synthesize the new DNA strand.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In eukaryotes, the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs is catalyzed by which of the following enzymes?
questions.solution:
In eukaryotes, there is a clear division of labor among the RNA polymerases in the nucleus.

RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, and 5.8S).

RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, the heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).

RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs (small nuclear RNAs).

DNA-dependent DNA polymerase is involved in DNA replication, not transcription.

Answer: RNA polymerase III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In eukaryotes, there is a clear division of labour among the RNA polymerases. Which of the following statements correctly links an RNA polymerase to its transcript and its subsequent post-transcriptional processing?
options: RNA polymerase II transcribes hnRNA, which undergoes capping, tailing, and splicing within the nucleus before being transported to the cytoplasm.
RNA polymerase I is responsible for transcribing hnRNA, which subsequently undergoes the removal of introns and joining of exons.
The transcripts produced by RNA polymerase III undergo the addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at their 5' end to become functional.
The primary transcript produced by RNA polymerase II is transported to the cytoplasm prior to the removal of introns and joining of exons.
questions.solution:
In eukaryotes, there are three types of RNA polymerases in the nucleus. RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs. RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of mRNA, called heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). RNA polymerase III is responsible for the transcription of tRNA, 5srRNA, and snRNAs.

The hnRNA undergoes post-transcriptional modifications including capping (addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end), tailing (addition of adenylate residues at the 3' end), and splicing (removal of introns and joining of exons). All these processes occur within the nucleus. Only the fully processed hnRNA, now called mRNA, is transported out of the nucleus to the cytoplasm for translation.

Therefore, the statement linking RNA polymerase II to hnRNA and its processing in the nucleus is correct. The other statements incorrectly assign hnRNA transcription to RNA polymerase I, incorrectly describe the processing of RNA polymerase III transcripts, or incorrectly state that splicing occurs in the cytoplasm.

Answer: RNA polymerase II transcribes hnRNA, which undergoes capping, tailing, and splicing within the nucleus before being transported to the cytoplasm.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A linear segment of B-DNA has a length of $34\mu\text{m}$. Assuming that a typical nucleosome contains $200$ base pairs of DNA helix, what is the maximum number of nucleosomes that can be formed from this segment?
questions.solution:
Length of the B-DNA segment $= 34\mu\text{m} = 34 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$

Distance between two consecutive base pairs $= 0.34\text{ nm} = 0.34 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$

Total number of base pairs in the segment $= \dfrac{34 \times 10^{-6}}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}} = 100,000\text{ bp}$

Number of base pairs in one typical nucleosome $= 200$

Maximum number of nucleosomes $= \dfrac{100,000}{200} = 500$

The option $100,000$ represents only the number of base pairs, missing the final step. Options with $50$ or $5000$ result from incorrect unit conversions.

Answer: $500$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A researcher aims to profile only the transcriptionally active genes of a newly discovered eukaryotic genome, deliberately ignoring all unexpressed sequences and non-coding DNA. Which of the following methodologies used during the Human Genome Project is most appropriate for this goal?
options: Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) profiling
Sanger sequencing of the whole genome
questions.solution:
During the Human Genome Project, two major methodologies were used. The approach that focuses exclusively on identifying all the genes that are expressed as RNA (transcriptionally active) is called Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs). This method effectively ignores unexpressed and non-coding DNA.

In contrast, Sequence Annotation involves taking a blind approach to sequence the entire genome (both coding and non-coding regions) and later assigning functions to different regions. VNTR profiling is a technique used in DNA fingerprinting, not for profiling active genes. Therefore, the researcher should adopt the Expressed Sequence Tags methodology.

Answer: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When E. coli is grown in a culture medium and lactose is added as the sole carbon source, it acts as an inducer for the lac operon. Which of the following represents the immediate molecular event that occurs after lactose enters the bacterial cell?
options: Lactose binds directly to the operator region, physically blocking the repressor.
Lactose binds to the repressor protein, causing a conformational change that inactivates it.
Lactose binds to RNA polymerase, activating it to transcribe the structural genes.
The i gene stops synthesizing the repressor protein in the presence of lactose.
questions.solution:
Lactose acts as an inducer in the lac operon. When lactose enters the E. coli cell, it binds to the repressor protein (which is synthesized constitutively by the i gene). This binding induces a conformational change in the repressor, rendering it inactive. The inactivated repressor can no longer bind to the operator region, allowing RNA polymerase access to the promoter to transcribe the structural genes.

Lactose does not bind to the operator or RNA polymerase, and the i gene continues to synthesize the repressor protein regardless of the presence of lactose.

Answer: Lactose binds to the repressor protein, causing a conformational change that inactivates it.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The genetic code is considered nearly universal, but exceptions exist in mitochondrial codons and some protozoans.
Reason (R): Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, which makes the genetic code degenerate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: The genetic code is nearly universal (for example, from bacteria to human, UUU would code for Phenylalanine), but NCERT explicitly notes that there are some exceptions to this rule in mitochondrial codons and in some protozoans.

Reason (R) is true: Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, and this property is known as the degeneracy of the genetic code.

Both statements are factually correct and represent independent properties of the genetic code. However, the degeneracy of the code is not the reason why there are exceptions to its universality. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a transcription unit, if the positions of the promoter and terminator are interchanged, which of the following will be the direct consequence?
options: The enzyme RNA polymerase will synthesize RNA in the $3' \rightarrow 5'$ direction.
The template strand will change but the coding strand will remain unaltered.
The definition of the coding and template strands will be reversed.
The structural gene will be transcribed into an identical mRNA sequence.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the presence of a promoter in a transcription unit defines the template and coding strands. The RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and initiates transcription.

If the positions of the promoter and terminator are interchanged, the RNA polymerase will bind at the opposite end and must transcribe the opposite strand to maintain its mandatory $5' \rightarrow 3'$ polymerization direction. Consequently, the definition of the coding and template strands is reversed.

The enzyme cannot synthesize RNA in the $3' \rightarrow 5'$ direction, and changing the template strand inevitably changes the coding strand. The resulting mRNA sequence will also be different, as it is transcribed from the newly defined template strand.

Answer: The definition of the coding and template strands will be reversed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements regarding the structural gene in a transcription unit and choose the incorrect one.
options: In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences within a structural gene are defined as introns.
The structural gene in a transcription unit is flanked by the promoter and terminator regions.
In eukaryotes, the structural gene is mostly monocistronic.
In bacteria or prokaryotes, the structural gene is predominantly polycistronic.
questions.solution:
In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences are defined as exons, not introns. Introns are intervening sequences that do not appear in mature or processed RNA.

The structural gene in a transcription unit is indeed flanked by the promoter (towards the $5'$ end of the coding strand) and the terminator (towards the $3'$ end). Furthermore, eukaryotic structural genes are mostly monocistronic, whereas prokaryotic structural genes are predominantly polycistronic. Therefore, the statement regarding introns being coding sequences is the incorrect one.

Answer: In eukaryotes, the coding sequences or expressed sequences within a structural gene are defined as introns.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding prokaryotic transcription.

List-IList-II
(A) RNA polymerase core enzyme(I) Initiation of transcription
(B) Sigma ($\sigma$) factor(II) Elongation of transcription
(C) Rho ($\rho$) factor(III) Termination of transcription

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, in prokaryotes, the DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is only capable of catalyzing the process of elongation. It associates transiently with the initiation factor ($\sigma$) to initiate transcription and with the termination factor ($\rho$) to terminate transcription. Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A point mutation occurs in an mRNA sequence, changing a single nitrogenous base in a codon. However, the amino acid sequence of the synthesized polypeptide chain remains completely unchanged. Which salient feature of the genetic code is primarily responsible for this observation?
options: The code is unambiguous and specific
The code is read in a contiguous fashion
questions.solution:
When a point mutation changes a single base in an mRNA codon but the resulting amino acid sequence remains unchanged, it indicates that the new codon codes for the same amino acid as the original codon (a silent mutation).

This observation is primarily due to the 'degenerate' nature of the genetic code, which means that some amino acids are coded by more than one codon.

The code being unambiguous means one codon codes for only one amino acid, which does not explain why two different codons can code for the same amino acid. Universality and contiguous reading are unrelated to this specific observation.

Answer: The code is degenerate

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the given statement and select the option that correctly fills the blanks (A) and (B).

In E. coli, the main enzyme for DNA replication is (A), which catalyses the polymerisation of deoxynucleotides strictly in the (B) direction.
questions.solution:
In prokaryotes like E. coli, the process of DNA replication is mainly catalysed by the enzyme DNA-dependent DNA polymerase.

This enzyme can catalyse polymerisation only in one direction, which is $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$.

DNA-dependent RNA polymerase is the main enzyme involved in transcription, not replication. The $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ direction is the polarity of the template strand that is read continuously, not the direction of polymerisation.

Answer: (A) DNA-dependent DNA polymerase, (B) $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In bacteria, RNA polymerase transiently binds with initiation factor ($\sigma$) and termination factor ($\rho$).
Reason (R): The core RNA polymerase enzyme is only capable of catalysing the process of elongation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
In prokaryotes, a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses the transcription of all types of RNA. The core RNA polymerase enzyme is only capable of catalysing the process of elongation. To initiate and terminate transcription, it must associate transiently with the initiation factor ($\sigma$) and termination factor ($\rho$), respectively.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) provides the correct explanation for why the core enzyme must bind to these factors in (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A very low level of expression of the lac operon has to be present in the cell all the time.
Reason (R): Lactose cannot enter the cell if permease is completely absent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. NCERT states that a very low (basal) level of expression of the lac operon must be present in the cell at all times.

Reason (R) is true. Permease, which is the product of the y gene of the lac operon, is required to transport lactose into the cell.

Reason (R) correctly explains Assertion (A). If the operon were completely shut off with absolutely zero expression, no permease would be present in the cell membrane. Without permease, lactose (the inducer) could not enter the cell to bind the repressor and induce the operon. Thus, a basal level of transcription is physiologically necessary.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II regarding a transcription unit in DNA.

List IList II
A. PromoterI. Located towards 3' end of the coding strand
B. TerminatorII. Has 3' → 5' polarity
C. Template strandIII. Located towards 5' end of the coding strand
D. Coding strandIV. Has 5' → 3' polarity

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In a transcription unit, all reference points are defined with respect to the coding strand.

The promoter is located towards the 5' end (upstream) of the coding strand.
The terminator is located towards the 3' end (downstream) of the coding strand.
The DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in only one direction, i.e., 5' → 3'. Therefore, the strand that has the polarity 3' → 5' acts as a template, and is called the template strand.
The other strand, which has the polarity 5' → 3' and the sequence same as RNA (except thymine at the place of uracil), is referred to as the coding strand.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During DNA replication, a replication fork exposes two template strands: Strand A with a polarity of $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ and Strand B with a polarity of $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$. Which of the following statements correctly identifies the strand that undergoes continuous synthesis and provides the correct reason?
options: Synthesis is continuous on Strand B because DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ direction.
Synthesis is continuous on Strand A because DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ direction.
Synthesis is continuous on Strand B because DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction.
Synthesis is continuous on Strand A because DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction.
questions.solution:
DNA-dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation only in one direction, that is $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$.

Consequently, on the template strand with $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ polarity (Strand A), the synthesis of the new strand can proceed continuously in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction.

On the other template strand with $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ polarity (Strand B), synthesis must occur discontinuously in small fragments (Okazaki fragments) because the enzyme can only add nucleotides in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction.

Answer: Synthesis is continuous on Strand A because DNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a eukaryotic transcription unit, the promoter is located towards the $5'$ end of the coding strand. Which strand's sequence does the newly formed hnRNA resemble, and to which end of this hnRNA are adenylate residues added during post-transcriptional processing?
questions.solution:
During transcription, the DNA strand with $3' \rightarrow 5'$ polarity acts as the template, while the strand with $5' \rightarrow 3'$ polarity is the coding strand. The newly synthesized hnRNA is complementary to the template strand, which means its sequence is identical to the coding strand (with uracil replacing thymine).

During post-transcriptional processing in eukaryotes, tailing involves the addition of $200-300$ adenylate residues to the $3'$ end of the hnRNA in a template-independent manner. Capping (addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate) occurs at the $5'$ end.

Therefore, the hnRNA resembles the coding strand, and adenylate residues are added to its $3'$ end.

Answer: Coding strand; $3'$ end

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List I with List II.

List I (Step in DNA fingerprinting)List II (Tool / Material used)
A. Digestion of DNAI. Autoradiography
B. Separation of DNA fragmentsII. Nitrocellulose or nylon membrane
C. Transferring of DNA fragmentsIII. Restriction endonucleases
D. Detection of hybridised DNAIV. Gel electrophoresis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - II, C - IV, D - I
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
questions.solution:
In DNA fingerprinting, the steps and their corresponding tools or materials are as follows:

Digestion of DNA is carried out by restriction endonucleases (A - III).

Separation of the digested DNA fragments is achieved by gel electrophoresis (B - IV).

Transferring (blotting) of the separated DNA fragments is done onto synthetic membranes such as nitrocellulose or nylon (C - II).

Detection of the hybridised DNA fragments is performed by autoradiography (D - I).

Therefore, the correct matching is A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I.

Answer: A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a eukaryotic cell, an enzyme 'X' synthesizes an RNA molecule that subsequently undergoes the addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at its 5'-end and adenylate residues at its 3'-end. Identify the enzyme 'X'.
questions.solution:
The addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5'-end (capping) and adenylate residues at the 3'-end (tailing) are post-transcriptional modifications specific to heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).

In eukaryotes, hnRNA is the precursor of mRNA and is transcribed by RNA polymerase II.

RNA polymerase I transcribes rRNAs (28S, 18S, 5.8S), and RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA, and snRNAs, which do not undergo this specific capping and polyadenylation process. Poly A polymerase is the enzyme responsible for adding the adenylate residues (tailing), not for synthesizing the initial RNA transcript.

Answer: RNA polymerase II

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Degenerate(I) One codon codes for only one amino acid
(B) Unambiguous(II) AUG codes for Methionine and acts as initiator
(C) Universal(III) Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon
(D) Dual Function(IV) UUU codes for Phenylalanine in bacteria as well as humans

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the salient features of the genetic code:
- Degenerate: Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon.
- Unambiguous and specific: One codon codes for only one amino acid.
- Universal: A specific codon codes for the same amino acid from bacteria to humans (e.g., UUU codes for Phenylalanine).
- Dual Function: AUG has dual functions; it codes for Methionine (met) and also acts as an initiator codon.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The codon UUU codes for only phenylalanine, illustrating that the genetic code is unambiguous and specific.
Reason (R): Some amino acids are coded by more than one codon, which makes the genetic code degenerate.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because a specific codon coding for only a single amino acid is the defining feature of the genetic code being unambiguous and specific. UUU codes exclusively for phenylalanine.

Reason (R) is also true because the phenomenon of a single amino acid being coded by multiple codons is known as degeneracy of the genetic code.

However, Reason (R) defines degeneracy, which is a completely different property from the unambiguous nature described in Assertion (A). Therefore, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the properties of genetic material:

(i) The 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA makes it reactive and easily degradable.
(ii) RNA is known to be catalytic, hence reactive.
(iii) The presence of thymine at the place of uracil confers additional stability to DNA.
(iv) Due to its double-stranded nature, DNA mutates at a much faster rate than RNA.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct as the 2'-OH group in the ribose sugar of every nucleotide makes RNA labile and easily degradable.

Statement (ii) is correct because RNA can act as a catalyst (ribozyme), which makes it more reactive than DNA.

Statement (iii) is correct as the presence of thymine instead of uracil provides additional chemical stability to DNA.

Statement (iv) is incorrect because DNA is structurally more stable and chemically less reactive than RNA; therefore, RNA mutates at a faster rate, not DNA. DNA's double-stranded nature and ability to undergo repair further reduce its mutation rate compared to RNA.

Thus, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the packaging of DNA helix in eukaryotes:
(i) The 'beads-on-string' structure in chromatin is packaged to form chromatin fibers.
(ii) Packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins called Non-Histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins.
(iii) Heterochromatin regions of chromatin are loosely packed and stain light.
(iv) A typical nucleosome contains 200 base pairs of DNA helix.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct as the 'beads-on-string' structure in chromatin is packaged to form chromatin fibers, which further coil and condense at the metaphase stage to form chromosomes.

Statement (ii) is correct because the packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins collectively referred to as Non-Histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins.

Statement (iii) is incorrect. Heterochromatin is densely packed and stains dark, whereas euchromatin is loosely packed and stains light.

Statement (iv) is correct as a typical nucleosome contains 200 base pairs of DNA helix.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
(I) In bacteria, a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses transcription of all types of RNA.
(II) Sigma ($\sigma$) factor is required for the termination of transcription in prokaryotes.
(III) In eukaryotes, there are at least three RNA polymerases in the nucleus.
(IV) Rho ($\rho$) factor transiently associates with RNA polymerase to initiate transcription.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (I) is correct as bacteria have a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase that catalyses the transcription of mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA.

Statement (II) is incorrect because the sigma ($\sigma$) factor is the initiation factor, not the termination factor.

Statement (III) is correct as eukaryotes have a clear division of labour with at least three RNA polymerases (I, II, and III) in the nucleus (in addition to the RNA polymerase found in organelles).

Statement (IV) is incorrect because the rho ($\rho$) factor is the termination factor, not the initiation factor.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding DNA fingerprinting and VNTRs:
A. Digestion of DNA is carried out by restriction endonucleases.
B. VNTR belongs to a class of satellite DNA referred to as mini-satellite.
C. Separation of DNA fragments is achieved by polymerase chain reaction (PCR).
D. The sensitivity of the DNA fingerprinting technique has been increased by the use of PCR.
E. The autoradiogram gives identical banding patterns for all individuals of a population.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: In DNA fingerprinting, the isolated DNA is digested by restriction endonucleases.

Statement B is correct: Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) belongs to a class of satellite DNA known as mini-satellite.

Statement C is incorrect: Separation of DNA fragments is done by gel electrophoresis, not by PCR. PCR is a technique used for the amplification of DNA.

Statement D is correct: The sensitivity of the technique has been increased by the use of PCR, allowing analysis to be performed even from the DNA of a single cell.

Statement E is incorrect: The autoradiogram gives a characteristic pattern of bands that differs from individual to individual in a population (except in the case of monozygotic twins).

Therefore, exactly three statements (A, B, and D) are correct.

Answer: Only three

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: DNA polymorphism forms the basis of genetic mapping and DNA fingerprinting. These polymorphisms arise due to mutations that accumulate generation after generation. What is the primary reason these mutations are able to accumulate in a population?
options: They immediately increase the reproductive fitness of the organism.
They are actively repaired by DNA polymerase before reproduction.
They occur in non-coding sequences and do not have any immediate impact on an individual's reproductive ability.
They are dominant lethal mutations that prevent the survival of the organism.
questions.solution:
Polymorphisms largely occur in non-coding DNA sequences. Mutations in these sequences may not have any immediate effect or impact on an individual's reproductive ability.

Because these mutations do not impair the organism's ability to reproduce, they are not eliminated by natural selection. Instead, they are passed on to subsequent generations and accumulate over time, forming the basis of DNA polymorphism.

Lethal mutations would be eliminated from the population, and actively repaired mutations would not persist to form polymorphisms. Furthermore, most non-coding mutations are neutral rather than immediately increasing reproductive fitness.

Answer: They occur in non-coding sequences and do not have any immediate impact on an individual's reproductive ability.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a mutant strain of E. coli, a mutation occurs in the $i$ gene of the lac operon, producing a modified repressor protein that has completely lost its ability to bind to the inducer (allolactose). What will be the transcription status of the structural genes ($z$, $y$, and $a$) in this mutant strain?
options: They will be transcribed constitutively, regardless of the presence or absence of lactose.
They will remain permanently switched off in both the presence and absence of lactose.
They will be transcribed normally only when lactose is present in the medium.
They will be transcribed only in the absence of lactose in the medium.
questions.solution:
The $i$ gene synthesises the repressor protein constitutively.

In a normal lac operon, the repressor binds to the operator region and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. When an inducer (lactose or allolactose) is present, it binds to the repressor, altering its conformation and inactivating it, which allows transcription to proceed.

If a mutation causes the repressor to lose its inducer-binding site, the inducer cannot bind to it. As a result, the mutant repressor will remain permanently active and continuously bound to the operator region.

Therefore, RNA polymerase will be permanently blocked, and the structural genes ($z$, $y$, and $a$) will never be transcribed, even if lactose is added to the medium.

Answer: They will remain permanently switched off in both the presence and absence of lactose.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the length of E. coli DNA is $1.36\text{ mm}$, calculate the number of base pairs in E. coli assuming the distance between two consecutive base pairs is $0.34\text{ nm}$.
questions.solution:
Length of DNA $= 1.36\text{ mm} = 1.36 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$

Distance between two consecutive base pairs $= 0.34\text{ nm} = 0.34 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$

Number of base pairs $= \dfrac{\text{Length of DNA}}{\text{Distance between consecutive base pairs}}$

$= \dfrac{1.36 \times 10^{-3}}{0.34 \times 10^{-9}} = 4 \times 10^6$

Note: While NCERT mentions the actual genome size of E. coli is $4.6 \times 10^6$ bp, the calculated value based on the given length of $1.36\text{ mm}$ is $4 \times 10^6$ bp. The option $4 \times 10^9$ results from incorrectly converting mm to m.

Answer: $4 \times 10^6$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A bacterial culture is treated with a specific chemical that completely inhibits the binding of the Rho ($\rho$) factor to the RNA polymerase enzyme, while the binding of the Sigma ($\sigma$) factor remains unaffected. What will be the most direct and immediate consequence on the transcription process in these bacteria?
options: The RNA polymerase will fail to initiate the process of transcription.
The RNA polymerase will fall off prematurely before elongating the transcript.
The RNA polymerase will fail to terminate transcription at the correct site.
The splicing of the newly synthesized RNA will not occur.
questions.solution:
In bacteria, the core RNA polymerase enzyme is capable of catalyzing elongation but requires transient association with specific factors for initiation and termination. The Sigma ($\sigma$) factor binds to RNA polymerase to initiate transcription, while the Rho ($\rho$) factor binds to it to terminate the process.

Since the chemical only inhibits the Rho factor and leaves the Sigma factor unaffected, initiation and elongation will proceed normally. However, without the Rho factor, the RNA polymerase will be unable to recognize the termination signal, leading to a failure to terminate transcription at the correct site.

Splicing is a feature of eukaryotes, not bacteria, making that option incorrect.

Answer: The RNA polymerase will fail to terminate transcription at the correct site.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The sequence of the coding strand in a transcription unit is the same as the transcribed RNA, except that thymine is replaced by uracil.

Reason (R): During transcription, the RNA polymerase reads and copies the coding strand to synthesize the mRNA.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true. By convention, the DNA strand with 5' to 3' polarity is called the coding strand. Its sequence is identical to the newly synthesized mRNA, with the only difference being the presence of thymine (T) in DNA and uracil (U) in RNA.

Reason (R) is false. During transcription, RNA polymerase binds to the promoter and reads the template strand (which has 3' to 5' polarity), not the coding strand. The coding strand does not code for anything and is displaced during the process. It is merely a reference strand for sequence nomenclature.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A newly discovered pathogen exhibits rapid antigenic variation and evolves at a very fast rate. Upon extraction, its genetic material is found to be highly labile and easily degradable. Based on these characteristics, identify the most likely nature of its genetic material and the specific chemical group primarily responsible for this lability.
questions.solution:
The pathogen exhibits rapid evolution, which implies a high mutation rate. According to NCERT, viruses having an RNA genome and a shorter life span mutate and evolve faster.

The chemical instability (lability) of RNA is primarily due to the presence of the 2'-OH (hydroxyl) group on the ribose sugar of every nucleotide. This reactive group makes RNA easily degradable and catalytic.

DNA lacks this 2'-OH group (having deoxyribose instead), making it chemically more stable. Therefore, the genetic material is RNA, and the lability is due to the 2'-OH group.

Answer: RNA; 2'-OH group

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the packaging of DNA helix.

List-IList-II
(A) DNA(I) Lysine and Arginine
(B) Histone octamer(II) Negatively charged polymer
(C) Basic amino acids(III) Required for higher level packaging
(D) NHC proteins(IV) Positively charged core

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
DNA is a negatively charged polymer due to the presence of phosphate groups.

Histones are organized to form a unit of eight molecules called a histone octamer, which acts as a positively charged core.

Histones acquire their positive charge because they are rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine.

The packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins collectively referred to as Non-Histone Chromosomal (NHC) proteins.

Therefore, the correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An E. coli strain develops a mutation in the operator region of the lac operon, altering its sequence such that the repressor protein can no longer bind to it. If these bacteria are cultured in a medium completely lacking lactose, what will be the expression status of the operon?
options: The structural genes will not be transcribed because lactose is absent.
Only the i gene will be transcribed, while structural genes remain repressed.
The z, y, and a genes will be transcribed continuously.
RNA polymerase will be unable to bind to the promoter region.
questions.solution:
The lac operon is normally under negative regulation. The i gene continuously synthesizes the repressor protein, which binds to the operator region to block RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes (z, y, and a) when lactose is absent.

In this mutant strain, the operator region is altered so the repressor cannot bind to it. Since the repressor cannot block the operator, RNA polymerase will have continuous access to the promoter. This results in the continuous (constitutive) transcription of the z, y, and a genes, regardless of whether lactose is present or absent in the medium.

Answer: The z, y, and a genes will be transcribed continuously.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the structural parameters of B-DNA and human genome lengths.

List-IList-II
A. Distance between consecutive base pairsI. $3.4$ nm
B. Pitch of B-DNA helixII. $0.34$ nm
C. Length of haploid human DNAIII. $2.2$ m
D. Length of diploid human DNAIV. $1.1$ m

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In a B-DNA double helix, the distance between two consecutive base pairs is $0.34$ nm, while the pitch of the helix (one complete turn) is $3.4$ nm.

The length of DNA is calculated by multiplying the total number of base pairs by the distance between consecutive base pairs.

For a haploid human genome ($3.3 \times 10^9$ bp):
Length $= 3.3 \times 10^9 \times 0.34 \times 10^{-9}$ m $\approx 1.1$ m.

For a diploid human genome ($6.6 \times 10^9$ bp):
Length $= 6.6 \times 10^9 \times 0.34 \times 10^{-9}$ m $\approx 2.2$ m.

Thus, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Viruses having RNA genome and shorter life span mutate and evolve faster.
Reason (R): The 2'-OH group present at every nucleotide in RNA makes it labile, catalytic and prone to faster mutation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, viruses having an RNA genome and a shorter life span mutate and evolve faster. This is because RNA is unstable and mutates at a faster rate.

The primary biochemical reason for this instability is the presence of a reactive 2'-OH group on the ribose sugar of every nucleotide, which makes RNA labile and easily degradable. RNA is also known to be catalytic, hence reactive. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Histone proteins tightly associate with the DNA double helix to form the core of a nucleosome.
Reason (R): Histones are rich in basic amino acid residues like lysine and arginine, which carry positive charges in their side chains.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because the positively charged histone octamer binds tightly with the negatively charged DNA to form a structure called the nucleosome.

Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A). Histones acquire their positive charge because they are rich in basic amino acids, lysine and arginine. Both of these amino acid residues carry positive charges in their side chains.

This electrostatic attraction between the positively charged histones and the negatively charged DNA is the exact reason they associate tightly to form the nucleosome core.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: For an inheritable mutation to be classified as a DNA polymorphism in a human population, the variant allele must occur at a locus with a frequency:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, allelic sequence variation has traditionally been described as a DNA polymorphism if more than one variant (allele) at a locus occurs in human population with a frequency greater than $0.01$.

If an inheritable mutation is observed in a population at this high frequency, it is referred to as DNA polymorphism.

Frequencies like $0.1$ or $0.001$ are incorrect due to decimal shift errors, and the condition strictly requires the frequency to be 'greater than' $0.01$, making 'exactly $0.01$' incorrect.

Answer: Greater than $0.01$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding transcription:

(A) The DNA strand with $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ polarity acts as the template for RNA polymerase.
(B) The sequence of the coding strand is the same as the newly synthesized mRNA except that thymine is present in place of uracil.
(C) DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in the $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ direction.
(D) If the sequence of the coding strand is $5^{\prime}$-ATC-$3^{\prime}$, the mRNA produced will be $5^{\prime}$-UAG-$3^{\prime}$.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct: RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ direction, so the template strand must have $3^{\prime} \rightarrow 5^{\prime}$ polarity.

Statement (B) is correct: The coding strand has the same sequence and $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ polarity as the transcribed mRNA, with thymine (T) instead of uracil (U).

Statement (C) is incorrect: DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization only in one direction, that is, $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$.

Statement (D) is incorrect: The mRNA sequence is identical to the coding strand (with U replacing T). If the coding strand is $5^{\prime}$-ATC-$3^{\prime}$, the mRNA will be $5^{\prime}$-AUC-$3^{\prime}$, not $5^{\prime}$-UAG-$3^{\prime}$.

Therefore, exactly two statements ((A) and (B)) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of transcription in prokaryotes.

List-IList-II
A. Core RNA polymeraseI. Initiation
B. Sigma ($\sigma$) factorII. Elongation
C. Rho ($\rho$) factorIII. Termination


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase enzyme is intrinsically responsible for catalysing the elongation phase of transcription (A-II).

To initiate transcription, the core enzyme must associate transiently with the initiation factor, which is the sigma ($\sigma$) factor (B-I).

For the termination of transcription, the RNA polymerase associates transiently with the termination factor, known as the rho ($\rho$) factor (C-III).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the regulation of the lac operon in E. coli, a specific molecule binds to the repressor protein synthesized by the i gene. This interaction inactivates the repressor, preventing it from binding to the operator region. Identify this molecule.
questions.solution:
In the lac operon, the i gene continuously synthesizes the repressor protein. This repressor binds to the operator region, preventing RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes.

When lactose is present, it acts as an inducer. It binds to the repressor protein and induces a conformational change that inactivates it. The inactivated repressor can no longer bind to the operator, allowing RNA polymerase access to the promoter to initiate transcription.

Glucose does not act as an inducer for this operon. RNA polymerase is the transcribing enzyme, and the promoter is a DNA sequence, neither of which are molecules that bind to inactivate the repressor.

Answer: Lactose

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
An mRNA molecule has the following nucleotide sequence:

$5^{\prime}$-CGA UAC GGU UAA-$3^{\prime}$

What will be the sequence and polarity of the DNA coding strand from which this mRNA was transcribed?
questions.solution:
The coding strand of DNA has the same sequence and polarity ($5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$) as the transcribed mRNA, with the only difference being that DNA contains thymine (T) in place of uracil (U).

Given mRNA sequence: $5^{\prime}$-CGA UAC GGU UAA-$3^{\prime}$

Replacing uracil (U) with thymine (T) while maintaining the $5^{\prime} \rightarrow 3^{\prime}$ polarity gives the coding strand sequence: $5^{\prime}$-CGA TAC GGT TAA-$3^{\prime}$.

The sequence $3^{\prime}$-GCT ATG CCA ATT-$5^{\prime}$ represents the template strand, which is complementary and antiparallel to the mRNA.

Answer: $5^{\prime}$-CGA TAC GGT TAA-$3^{\prime}$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In bacteria, the core RNA polymerase enzyme is capable of independently initiating the process of transcription.

Reason (R): The core RNA polymerase is only capable of catalysing the process of elongation and must associate transiently with the initiation factor ($\sigma$) to initiate transcription.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is incorrect because the core RNA polymerase enzyme in bacteria cannot initiate transcription on its own.

Reason (R) is correct because the core RNA polymerase is inherently capable of catalysing only the process of elongation. To initiate transcription, it must associate transiently with the initiation factor ($\sigma$). This association confers the specificity required to bind to the promoter and initiate transcription.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the lac operon in E. coli:
A. Glucose or galactose cannot act as inducers for the lac operon.
B. Regulation of the lac operon by the repressor is referred to as positive regulation.
C. The $y$ gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to $\beta$-galactosides.
D. The repressor of the operon is synthesized from the $i$ gene only in the presence of lactose.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: NCERT explicitly states that glucose or galactose cannot act as inducers for the lac operon; only lactose or allolactose can.

Statement B is incorrect: Regulation of the lac operon by the repressor is referred to as negative regulation, because the repressor protein turns off the operon.

Statement C is correct: The $y$ gene codes for permease, an enzyme that increases the permeability of the cell to $\beta$-galactosides (lactose).

Statement D is incorrect: The repressor protein is synthesised constitutively (all the time) from the $i$ gene, not just in the presence of lactose.

Thus, exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Two

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) Sigma factor(I) $5'$ end of hnRNA
(B) Rho factor(II) $3'$ end of hnRNA
(C) Capping(III) Initiation of transcription
(D) Tailing(IV) Termination of transcription


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
In bacteria, the RNA polymerase transiently binds to the initiation factor, sigma ($\sigma$), to initiate transcription, and to the termination factor, rho ($\rho$), to terminate the process.

In eukaryotes, the primary transcript (hnRNA) undergoes post-transcriptional modifications. During capping, an unusual nucleotide (methyl guanosine triphosphate) is added to the $5'$ end of hnRNA. In tailing, adenylate residues (poly-A tail) are added at the $3'$ end in a template-independent manner.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match the genes of the lac operon in List-I with their respective protein products in List-II.

List-IList-II
(A) i gene(I) Transacetylase
(B) z gene(II) Permease
(C) y gene(III) $\beta$-galactosidase
(D) a gene(IV) Repressor protein

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene and three structural genes.

The i gene codes for the repressor protein of the lac operon.

The z gene codes for $\beta$-galactosidase, which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of lactose into galactose and glucose.

The y gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to $\beta$-galactosides.

The a gene codes for a transacetylase.

Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).

Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a transcription unit, the promoter is said to be located towards the $5'$-end of the structural gene.

Reason (R): The convention in defining the regions of a transcription unit is based on the polarity of the template strand.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because, by convention, the promoter is located towards the $5'$-end (upstream) of the structural gene.

Reason (R) is false because the convention in defining the regions of a transcription unit is based on the polarity of the coding strand, not the template strand. According to NCERT, all reference points while defining a transcription unit are made with respect to the coding strand, which has $5' \rightarrow 3'$ polarity.

Therefore, Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Answer: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the experiments conducted by Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty to determine the biochemical nature of the 'transforming principle', the addition of which of the following enzymes inhibited the transformation of R strain bacteria to S strain?
questions.solution:
Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty purified biochemicals (proteins, DNA, RNA, etc.) from the heat-killed S cells to see which ones could transform live R cells into S cells.

They discovered that protein-digesting enzymes (proteases) and RNA-digesting enzymes (RNases) did not affect transformation, so the transforming substance was not a protein or RNA.

Digestion with DNase did inhibit transformation, suggesting that the DNA caused the transformation. This proved that DNA is the hereditary material.

Answer: DNase

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Codons)List-II (Properties/Amino acids)
A. AUGI. Phenylalanine
B. UUUII. Terminator codon
C. UAAIII. Lysine
D. AAAIV. Dual function

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to the properties of the genetic code:

- AUG has dual functions. It codes for the amino acid Methionine and also acts as the initiator codon. (A matches with IV)
- UUU codes for the amino acid Phenylalanine. (B matches with I)
- UAA, UAG, and UGA are stop or terminator codons that do not code for any amino acid. (C matches with II)
- AAA and AAG code for the amino acid Lysine. (D matches with III)

Thus, the correct matching is A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

Answer: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If a highly specific inhibitor completely blocks the activity of RNA polymerase II in a eukaryotic cell, which of the following processes or products will be most immediately and directly absent?
questions.solution:
In eukaryotes, there is a clear division of labour among the three nuclear RNA polymerases.

RNA polymerase II is specifically responsible for transcribing the precursor of mRNA, which is known as heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA). Therefore, inhibiting RNA polymerase II directly halts hnRNA formation.

Synthesis of 28S and 18S rRNAs is carried out by RNA polymerase I, while tRNA synthesis is mediated by RNA polymerase III. Peptide bond formation is a part of translation, which would eventually stop due to a lack of mature mRNA, but it is not the immediate and direct product of RNA polymerase II activity.

Answer: Formation of heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding transcription:

(a) DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in only one direction, that is, 5' → 3'.
(b) The DNA strand with polarity 3' → 5' acts as the template.
(c) The coding strand has the polarity 5' → 3' and its sequence is identical to the transcribed RNA except for having thymine in place of uracil.
(d) The terminator is located towards the 3' end of the coding strand.

How many of the given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is correct. DNA-dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerisation in the 5' → 3' direction only.

Statement (b) is correct. Since polymerisation occurs in the 5' → 3' direction, the template strand must have 3' → 5' polarity.

Statement (c) is correct. The coding strand has 5' → 3' polarity. Its sequence is the same as the newly synthesised RNA, except that DNA contains thymine (T) whereas RNA contains uracil (U).

Statement (d) is correct. The terminator region is located downstream, which is defined as towards the 3' end of the coding strand.

Therefore, all four statements are correct.

Answer: Four

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: During the process of transcription in bacteria, a stage is reached where the nascent RNA falls off and the RNA polymerase also separates from the DNA, marking the end of the process. Which of the following transiently associates with the RNA polymerase to facilitate this specific event?
questions.solution:
In prokaryotes, the core RNA polymerase is only capable of catalysing the elongation step of transcription.

To terminate the process, the RNA polymerase must transiently associate with a termination factor, known as the $\rho$ (rho) factor, when it reaches the terminator region. This association alters the specificity of the enzyme, causing the nascent RNA and the polymerase to fall off the DNA.

The $\sigma$ (sigma) factor is required for initiation, not termination. The core enzyme cannot terminate transcription on its own, and DNA helicase is involved in unwinding DNA during replication, not transcription termination.

Answer: $\rho$ (rho) factor

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The lac operon is completely turned off in the absence of an inducer, with absolutely no basal level of expression.
Reason (R): Lactose cannot enter the bacterial cell if permease is completely absent.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
NCERT explicitly states that a very low level of expression of the lac operon has to be present in the cell all the time. Therefore, the Assertion is false because the operon is never completely shut down with zero expression.

This basal level of expression ensures that a small amount of permease (the product of the $y$ gene) is always available in the cell membrane. The Reason is true because permease is essential for the transport of lactose into the cell. If permease were completely absent, lactose from the surrounding medium could never enter the cell to bind to the repressor and fully turn on the operon.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A segment of eukaryotic chromatin contains exactly $2000$ base pairs of DNA. Assuming typical packaging, what is the total number of individual histone protein molecules present in the core octamers of this segment?
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, a typical nucleosome contains $200$ base pairs (bp) of DNA helix.

First, calculate the number of nucleosomes in the given segment:
Number of nucleosomes = $\dfrac{2000 \text{ bp}}{200 \text{ bp per nucleosome}} = 10$ nucleosomes.

Next, recall that the core of each nucleosome is formed by a histone octamer, which consists of $8$ histone protein molecules.

Total number of histone molecules in the core octamers = $10 \text{ nucleosomes} \times 8 \text{ histones per core} = 80$ histone molecules.

The value $10$ represents only the number of nucleosomes. The value $90$ incorrectly includes the H1 histone (which is outside the core octamer) for each nucleosome. The value $160$ would result from incorrectly assuming $100$ bp per nucleosome.

Answer: $80$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of the lac operon.

List-IList-II
(A) i gene(I) Interacts with repressor protein to inactivate it
(B) Operator(II) Binding site for RNA polymerase
(C) Promoter(III) Synthesizes repressor constitutively
(D) Inducer(IV) Binding site for the active repressor

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The i gene is a regulatory gene that is expressed constitutively to synthesize the repressor protein. Therefore, (A) matches with (III).

The operator region is the specific DNA sequence where the active repressor protein binds to prevent transcription. Therefore, (B) matches with (IV).

The promoter is the sequence where RNA polymerase binds to initiate transcription of the structural genes. Therefore, (C) matches with (II).

The inducer (lactose or allolactose) binds to the repressor protein, inactivating it so that it can no longer bind to the operator. Therefore, (D) matches with (I).

Swapping the binding sites of RNA polymerase and the repressor is a common error, but RNA polymerase always binds to the promoter.

Answer: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the lac operon in E. coli:

List-IList-II
A. LactoseI. Codes for the repressor protein
B. Repressor proteinII. Binding site for the repressor
C. OperatorIII. Binds to the operator to prevent transcription
D. i geneIV. Acts as an inducer to inactivate the repressor

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The i gene is a regulatory gene that constitutively codes for the repressor protein (D matches I).

The repressor protein binds to the operator region of the operon to prevent transcription by RNA polymerase (B matches III).

The operator is the specific DNA sequence adjacent to the promoter where the repressor binds (C matches II).

Lactose acts as an inducer by binding to the repressor protein and inactivating it, thereby turning the operon on (A matches IV).
